events.title: Factory Workshop
events.description:
Shipping with the Factory Droid SDK

"Droid is the coding agent behind Factory's CLI, desktop app, and web platform. With the Droid SDK, you can now put Droid inside your own projects. It plans the steps, uses tools, edits files, and runs commands. You decide when it runs, what it can access, and what it builds.

In this hands-on workshop, we'll go from an empty folder to a working agent-powered app in under an hour. You'll learn how to:
- Install the SDK in TypeScript (npm install @factory/droid-sdk) or Python (pip install droid-sdk) and start your first Droid session.
- Give Droid a task, stream its progress, and handle its results in your app.
- Control what Droid can access: which files, which tools, and which commands.
- Trigger Droid from your own code, like a button, a webhook, a cron job, or a chat message.
- Avoid the common mistakes that cost hackathon teams hours.

We'll end with a live build and a look at what wins our track. Bring a laptop and an idea, or leave with one."

events.title: Figma Workshop
events.description:
From Canvas to Shipped: How to Differentiate in the Age of AI

"This workshop is designed for students who want to learn how to use Figma Agent to move from prototype to ship, even with tight hackathon timelines. You’ll be guided through describing what you want, steering the agent toward better results, and editing and refining what it creates on the canvas.

Using AI as a creative partner while keeping your own point of view, this session will help you build faster without losing the craft, so your work stands out instead of blending in. No design background required, making it a great fit for first-time Figma users, and you’ll leave ready to build a standout project for CalHacks 13.0."

events.title: Hyphenate Workshop
events.description:
Beyond Agentic Harnesses: Engineering the Autonomous Enterprise

Harnesses made agents capable; the frontier is making them autonomous inside the systems and teams that run a company. We've been doing it in finance, where a single economic event can ripple across a dozen systems and people, and every decision has to stand up to scrutiny long after it's made. We'll take apart how: designing the environment an autonomous system acts in, keeping state across long horizons, orchestrating agents and humans as one team, and building in permissions and traceability from day one. It's hands-on and interactive, so bring a laptop and build along. You'll leave with a blueprint for autonomous systems an enterprise team would bring on board, and a head start on our track.

events.title: Elastic Workshop
events.description:
Build an Agent That Does the Research: Context Engineering with Elasticsearch

Build an AI agent that searches papers and project docs, compares approaches, and creates research briefs backed by sources. events.title: SpaceXAI Workshop
events.description:
Build Your Entire Internship Application Stack in 30 Minutes

What you'll build:

A portfolio website. You'll set up a project in Cursor, have the agent build your site, and deploy it so it's live on the web.
A headshot generator. You'll connect the Grok Imagine API with your API key and turn a casual photo into a professional headshot.
An interview practice tool. Built on the Grok Voice API, it asks you interview questions out loud and responds to your answers. We'll debug it live so you can see how Cursor helps you fix errors fast.
Then we'll show you Grok Bot, an AI assistant that works for you in the background. It has its own computer and browser, connects to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion and Slack, and can run tasks on a schedule. For your internship search, that means it can:

Find new openings that match the roles you want and keep a running tracker of where you've applied
Check job boards for you every morning and message you when something new shows up
Research a company and its recruiters before you reach out
Draft cover letters and outreach emails for you to review and send
Put interview dates and deadlines on your calendar and remind you before they come up
You don't need experience with AI APIs. If you've written some code before, you can follow along. Install Cursor before you come, and we'll hand out API credits so you can keep building with Grok all weekend.

events.title: Bright Data Workshop - The Unfair Advantage: Live Web Data
events.description:
The data your project needs often lives on sites that fight automation: Indeed, Glassdoor, Yelp, Booking.com, and Google search results. In 50 minutes, you'll learn to turn public web content into structured data your project can use.

We'll build Intern Intel together: an agent that finds internship listings on Indeed and Glassdoor, combines them into one table, removes duplicates, and helps you filter by role and location. Along the way, you'll see how Bright Data handles web access and extraction, and how your app turns that data into something useful.

We'll build live using Bright Data's MCP server in Claude Code or Cursor, then show how to adapt the workflow to your hackathon idea. You'll leave with a starter repo, including Python, JavaScript, and CLI examples you can reuse.

Code along or just watch. No scraping experience needed.

REQUIREMENTS
To code along:
- Bring a laptop with Claude Code or Cursor installed, signed in, and working.
- Create a Bright Data account and connect its MCP server before the session. Follow the setup guide linked on the event page.
- Have Git installed, or download the starter repo as a ZIP.
- Optional: Python or Node.js to run the standalone examples; tested versions will be listed in the repo.
- Optional: a phone hotspot as a Wi-Fi backup.

events.title: Moss Workshop
events.description:
Retrieval in 6‑7ms w/ Moss

A hands-on workshop on with Moss, a semantic search library built in Rust and WebAssembly. Participants will build an app that runs low-latency semantic search locally, fast enough to keep up with user input in real time. Topics include creating and loading a vector index, semantic and hybrid (keyword + embedding) search, metadata filtering, and how fast local retrieval applies to RAG pipelines, AI agents, and voice assistants. Participants leave with a starter project they can build on during the hackathon.

events.title: Apify Workshop
events.description:
Apify is your superpower for hackathons.

Learn how to get structured, real-time data from almost any website using Apify actors, and plug it into your project through the API, the CLI, or MCP for AI agents. You’ll also see a new way to work with Apify: describing the actor you need in plain English and having AI build and deploy a custom Actor for you in chat. Bring your laptop to claim $200 in free credits with code APIFY_CAL_HACKS, run your first Actor, grab some Apify swag, and leave with a working data pipeline for your hack.

Discover the latest trends in tokenization, real-time risk scoring, and ethical AI practices that keep payment networks safe and seamless. This session is perfect for anyone curious about the intersection of cutting-edge technology and financial security. Don’t miss this opportunity to learn more about Visa’s role in driving innovation and building trust in the global payment ecosystem.

events.title: Anthropic Workshop
events.description:
Building Agents & Multi-Agent Teams with Claude

In this workshop, three Anthropic engineers show you how to build with multiple Claude agents: how many your project needs, what each one should own, and when adding one more is a bad idea.

You'll see the problems that hit first-time hackers over 36 hours, from workflows that eat your credits to agents overwriting each other's code, with fixes you can use in Claude Code that same night. You'll also get a look at what has recently improved in how Claude agents work together, and how to use it in your build.

events.title: Meta Workshop
events.description:
From Chatbots to Agent Teams: Agentic Engineering at Meta

Most people use AI like a search box. Meta engineers use it like a team.

In this hands-on workshop, you'll go behind the scenes on how engineers at Meta actually build with AI today -- moving past copy-paste chatbots to orchestrating agents that write, review, and verify real code. Then you'll put it into practice and build something real
yourself.

You'll walk away knowing:
- The four levels of agentic AI -- and where you land on the curve
- How Meta engineers turn AI from an adviser into a teammate
- Hands-on time with Muse Code, Meta's CLI coding agent -- take an idea to working software in under an hour

Who it's for: student engineers who already code and want to go from using AI to directing it.

events.title: Fetch.ai Workshop
events.description:
Build, Deploy & Monetise AI Agents with Fetch.ai

This hands-on workshop focuses on turning ideas into real, discoverable AI agents. We’ll walk you through practical use cases and showcase project ideas that align with the hackathon challenge. From designing agentic workflows to registering agents on Agentverse and making them discoverable via ASI:One, you’ll see the full lifecycle in action. Beyond building, we’ll dive into monetisation, integrating Chat Protocol and Payment Protocol, exposing your agents to real users, and transforming capabilities into revenue-generating services.By the end of the session, you’ll have a clear blueprint for creating, deploying, and monetising AI agents that solve real-world problems and a strong foundation to build a winning hackathon project.

Join Convex for a quick intro to our reactive backend platform, followed by a live demo of how to build full-stack apps with AI coding agents. We’ll walk through how Convex fits into your stack, show you what’s possible, and leave time for Q&A so you can get back to building.
